news.title: U-17 World Cup: Fans hail Flamingos semi-final qualification
news.lede: Nigerian football fans have praised the Flamingos following their qualification for the semi-finals of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco, after a hard-fought 1-0 victory over Venezuela on Sunday. Azeezat Oduntan converted a late penalty in the 89th minute to send Nigeria into the last four, where they will face Brazil on Wednesday for a place in the final. Fans said the team had lived up to expectations despite losing their opening group-stage match to Poland. Read Also: Flamingos edge out Venezuela to reach U-17 World Cup semi-finals.

news.title: From World Cup Heartbreak to Olympic Glory: Neymar's Golden Night at Rio 2016
news.lede: Brazil had produced some of football’s greatest players and won five FIFA World Cups, but one major achievement had continued to elude the nation. Olympic men’s football gold remained missing from their collection, despite three appearances in the final. In front of a passionate home crowd at the Maracana in Rio de Janeiro, Neymar finally helped bring that wait to an end in August 2016. news.title: Dazn secures exclusive deal on global streaming rights for 2029 Club World Cup
news.lede: Deal deepens company’s relationship with Fifa. Dazn paid $1bn for global rights for the 2025 tournament. Dazn has secured an exclusive option for global streaming rights for the next men’s Club World Cup in 2029 in a development that deepens its partnership with Fifa. The Saudi Arabia-backed streaming company came to Fifa’s aid before the inaugural 32-team Club World Cup in the United States last year by agreeing to pay $1bn for global rights for the tournament after many linear broadcasters and other streamers had declined to bid.

news.title: Will AFC Asian Cup 2027 be postponed amid Houthi attacks and threats in Saudi Arabia?
news.lede: The upcoming edition of the AFC Asian Cup is scheduled to take place in Saudi Arabia between January 7 and February 5 next year. Saudi Arabia, which will host the FIFA World Cup in 2034, will have an opportunity to use the Asian Cup as a dress rehearsal for the World Cup, which has expanded to a 48-team showpiece from this year. However, with the Houthis launching missiles and drone attacks on three Saudi airports — killing 22 people and injuring more than 380 others — the chances of the Asian Cup taking place in the Gulf nation look uncertain. Japan Football Association president Tsuneyasu Miyamoto expressed his doubts that the tournament will go ahead as originally planned.
